text.p: Germany sent 24 Bosnian refugees back to Sarajevo on Wednesday, including the first single people without criminal records to be repatriated since it decided more than 300,000 refugees would have to return.
Despite protests from some politicians and refugee groups, the deportees were put on a chartered Fokker 27 plane in the cargo area of Munich airport, out of sight of media cameras and reporters.

A spokesman for the Bavarian Interior Ministry said 15 of the group had been convicted of crimes. Nine others who had no record and had been living on social security in Germany, were all skilled craftsmen.

He said 22 of the refugees had lived in Bavaria and were aged between 22 and 38. The other two were from Baden-Wuerttemberg state. Up to now Bavaria has deported 13 Bosnians, all of whom had been convicted of crimes.
The ministry spokesman said by the end of the year a total of 100 refugees, out of 67,000 in Bavaria, would be sent back.

Germany and Bosnia signed an agreement last month covering the repatriation of more than 300,000 refugees from the conflict in former Yugoslavia and said they hoped many would start returning soon of their own free will.
But Interior Minister Manfred Kanther said Germany would send back those who refused to go voluntarily, starting with single adults and married couples without children.
The plan intends for the first phase of 70,000 to 90,000 refugees to be back in Bosnia by June 30, 1997.
Bavarian Green party chairwoman Ruth Paulig said the repatriation would endanger the fragile peace in Bosnia if people were sent back to live in rooms rather than in proper accomodation.
The Pro Asyl refugee organisation described the repatriation as "inhumane".
During the Balkan war, Germany welcomed more refugees than the rest of the European Union put together -- more than 400,000 from former Yugoslavia, 80 percent of them from Bosnia.
Germany's federal government and 16 states agreed earlier this year that refugees could be forced to go home from October 1 if they refused to go voluntarily.
